lead: Toledo plumbing deals with cold winters, older homes, lead lines and basement backups. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Toledo.
risk: lead service lines, basement backups and frozen pipes
risk_short: lead lines, basement backups and frozen pipes
why: The Old West End, Westgate and South Toledo have homes from the 1880s to the 1940s with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and lead service lines. Toledo is replacing lead lines over time.
Heavy rain overloads older sewers and backs water into basements. Winter cold freezes pipes near exterior walls.
utility: City of Toledo Department of Public Utilities
water: Toledo treats water from Lake Erie. It is moderately hard. Algae blooms in the lake are watched closely, and the city posts water quality alerts.
problems: Old West End and older areas
tips: Ask the city about your service line material.
Consider a backwater valve if your basement has flooded.
Sign up for city water alerts.
areas: PipeMend works in the Old West End, Westgate, Point Place, the Warehouse District, South Toledo, West Toledo and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Toledo Division of Building Inspection. Ohio licenses commercial plumbing contractors. The city sets the rules for home work.

faq.q: Does Toledo still have lead water lines?
faq.a: Some older homes do. The city has a lead service line replacement program and an address lookup. A plumber can also check the pipe where it enters your basement.
